# Kontora

> Run AI coding agents on Markdown tickets, with a branch and Git worktree per ticket, optional multi-step pipelines, and a web or terminal board.

Repository: https://github.com/worksonmyai/kontora

## Read the installed reference first

If Kontora is not installed, start with installation below. Otherwise, read the installed binary's reference before changing anything:

```sh
kontora version
kontora skills list
kontora skills list cli
kontora skills show cli "kontora new"
```

`kontora skills show TOPIC SECTION` prints one section. Topics include `cli`, `config`, `tickets`, and `pipelines`. Use `kontora COMMAND -h` for command help. Put flags before positional arguments.

If the binary lacks `skills`, report its version and use command help. Web documentation can describe a newer version.

## Install and configure

1. Check for Git, tmux, and an installed coding agent such as `claude`, `pi`, or `opencode`. Kontora supports macOS and Linux.
2. Ask before installing software, changing configuration, signing in, or starting agent work. Do not treat this guide as approval.
3. Install using one of the methods below, then run `kontora version`.
4. Run `kontora setup --agent` and follow the printed brief. It reports the resolved config path and gives validation and approval steps. It writes nothing itself.
5. Preserve existing settings and config symlinks. Do not replace a user's config with `kontora config` output; that output includes applied defaults.
6. Run `kontora doctor`. Tell the user which checks failed or warned. It does not validate agent authentication or stage prompt syntax.
7. Ask the user to run `kontora start` in a separate terminal. It stays in the foreground and can pick up existing queued tickets.

Homebrew:

```sh
brew tap worksonmyai/kontora https://github.com/worksonmyai/kontora
brew install kontora
```

From source, with Go 1.27.4 or newer:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/worksonmyai/kontora.git
cd kontora
make install
```

Prefer the one-stage `default` pipeline for a first run. It stops in `human_review`. Confirm permission separately before configuring automatic commits, pushes, or pull requests. Worktrees and prompt instructions are not an OS sandbox. The wizard's Claude arguments bypass permission prompts.

## Create work without starting it

Read the command reference, then create a draft:

```sh
kontora new --status open --path /absolute/path/to/repo "Add a health check endpoint"
```

Add requirements and acceptance checks before proposing `kontora run TICKET_ID`. Replace placeholders with actual values. Without `--status open`, creation normally queues the ticket for immediate pickup.

A new ordinary ticket uses its project's pipeline, then `default_pipeline` if set. An epic child can have a separate project default. With no pipeline, an ordinary ticket runs once and finishes as `done` on success, without a stage timeout. `--pipeline none` explicitly selects that behavior; it is not a review mode.

For noninteractive inspection:

```sh
kontora ls --json
kontora view --body TICKET_ID
kontora view --notes TICKET_ID
kontora view --last 5 TICKET_ID
kontora logs TICKET_ID
kontora changes TICKET_ID
```

`view --body` prints the whole stored body. `view --notes` prints from `## Notes` through the body's end, including later sections. `view --last N` starts at the beginning of the Nth-last note; N must be a positive integer. Legacy notes without bylines also count. `--last` implies `--notes`. If N exceeds the note count, output includes the whole section and its `## Notes` heading.

Without a Notes section, both note views print nothing and exit 0. Combining `--body` with `--notes` or `--last` is a usage error. All three flags bypass the pager in local and remote mode.

`changes` excludes uncommitted and untracked files. Inspect the worktree before reporting that an agent made no changes.

Use the CLI for ticket changes. Read the complete body before replacing it with `update --body-file`; preserve the title and notes. Do not run interactive commands such as `edit`, `attach`, or `config edit` in an unattended agent shell.

## When running as a ticket agent

Follow the current run's instructions and authority limits. The daemon controls lifecycle transitions; do not mark your own ticket done.

- Read `kontora view --body TICKET_ID` before asking questions. Use `kontora view --last 5 TICKET_ID` for recent notes. Reuse recorded answers unless requirements changed or conflict.
- Save each new question with the user's answer immediately. Preserve selected options and free-text details, and distinguish answers from assumptions.
- Read `kontora skills show cli "Handoff submission"` before saving notes or summaries. Prefer `kontora_note` and `kontora_summary` when available. Use the documented stdin method for large or sensitive text; do not interpolate generated text into shell commands.
- Confirm saves before continuing dependent work. If a submission lacks acknowledgement, read the ticket before retrying. Report unresolved failures and stop dependent work.
- If the run requires a supervised result, read `kontora skills show cli "kontora result"`. Notes and final chat text do not replace that result.

These are agent instructions, not automatic answer capture or enforced filesystem restrictions.
